p: With so many rescued buildings to choose from, it's fun to give everyone in the group a mission. Let the kids hunt down the phone boxes and see how many different styles they can count, while the grown-ups make for the oldest timber-framed house and try to imagine the Bromsgrove streets it once stood on. Someone always ends up fascinated by the prefab, which shows how families in post-war Birmingham were thrilled to get a fitted kitchen and an indoor bathroom.

The windmill is a particular favourite. It's a post mill, the type where the whole body of the mill turns to face the wind, and when the sails are turning it's a cracking sight against the Worcestershire sky. Keep an eye out for event days too, when demonstrations, crafts and themed activities bring extra life to the buildings.

Bring a picnic on a fine day, as there's grass to spread out on, and pack waterproofs if the clouds are looking heavy. Wear shoes you're happy to get a bit muddy, especially outside the summer months.

To stretch the day out, the Lickey Hills Country Park, on the edge of Bromsgrove towards Birmingham, has woodland, heathland and great views from Beacon Hill. Hanbury Hall, a grand National Trust house with formal gardens, is a short drive south-west, and the canal at Tardebigge, with its long flight of locks climbing the hillside, makes for a peaceful towpath walk with plenty of narrowboats to wave at.
